content.title: About
content.content: Coarse and semi‑coarse semolina flour is a dry grain product obtained from wheat after milling and sieving. The coarse variety has larger granules, while the semi‑coarse is slightly finer. Both are widely used for porridges, doughs, breading and baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Semolina is made from hard wheat varieties that are high in protein.
Coarse semolina is a staple in many Eastern European and Middle Eastern dishes such as semolina porridge and dumplings.
Semi‑coarse semolina is often added to bread and pastry doughs to give a light, airy crumb.
Semolina has a higher glycemic index than whole‑grain flour.
In several countries semolina is considered a basic pantry item.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Semolina provides a quick source of energy due to its high starch content.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Hard wheat used for semolina contains about 12 % protein, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, riboflavin and niacin in semolina help metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Semolina supplies iron, magnesium and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The fine granule size makes semolina easy on the stomach, especially when cooked as a porridge.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with gluten intolerance or wheat allergy may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large servings can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, which is a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or heat treatment can mitigate this.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Semolina is used to make porridges, dumplings, breading, and dough for breads, rolls and desserts. Coarse semolina is often boiled until soft, while semi‑coarse is added to doughs for a lighter texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store semolina in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep it in the refrigerator to prevent mold and fat rancidity.
